answer: Tie each identity to one professional license. First, onboarding checks the number against the registry of the bar or medical board, and one license backs one agent only. Second, the registry is re-checked each epoch, and a revoked or duplicated license kills the identity. Third, a random audit demands an extract, with yearly renewal. Earning 1,000 licenses costs about 300 dollars a year each in renewals plus 2,000 dollars in exam fees, over 2.3 million dollars. A sybil fleet cannot forge a profession: its island of paper licenses sinks once the kernel of real credentials is checked.
